Strategy: Combine parent one's sharp tight-fit preference with parent two's residual windows in one decreasing rule with jumps: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual, so near-exact fills dominate; residuals in [28,48] gain a 30 bonus, preserving leftovers that still fit medium items; residuals in [8,22] lose 30, avoiding awkward small leftovers; all other residuals score minus residual. Ranking changes at the window boundaries; it may fail if the preserved window rarely matches future item sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else (30 - (r - item) if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else (-30 - (r - item) if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else -(r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Fuse parent one's triangular peak with parent two's alternating bands: place two triangular peaks centered on the even-band centers 25 and 45, each rising to 30 and falling to 20 at its edges, with a valley near 35. The rule preserves residuals near either peak size while still preferring tight fits elsewhere through the minus-residual base. Ranking changes inside the two peak windows; it may fail if future items do not cluster near 25 or 45.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 - abs((r - item) - 25) if 15 <= r - item <= 35 else 0) + (30 - abs((r - item) - 45) if 35 < r - item <= 55 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents' window rules into a graded bonus: residuals in [30,45] earn 25, 15, or 5 depending on whether the item size is 1, 2, or 0 modulo 3, blending both parents' gates; residuals in [8,22] lose 20, using the wider penalized window. The bonus size now varies with the item class, so ranking changes both across windows and across item residues; it may fail if item residues carry no information about future sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 and item % 3 == 1 else (15 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 and item % 3 == 2 else (5 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else 0))) - (20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge both parents' windows into one stepped profile with parent two's item-scaled magnitudes: residuals in [28,45] gain item/2, residuals in (22,28) gain item/4, and residuals in [6,22] lose item/2, using the union of both parents' window edges. The score rises in steps with residual size inside the useful range, so ranking changes at each step boundary; it may fail if the step edges do not line up with real future item sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (item / 2 if 28 <= r - item <= 45 else (item / 4 if 22 < r - item < 28 else 0)) - (item / 2 if 6 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's band parity with parent two's windows and item-scaled penalty: residuals in [28,48] earn 30 in even 10-wide bands and 15 in odd bands, so the preserved window prefers its edges over its middle; residuals in [8,22] lose item/2, scaling the punishment with the item at stake. Ranking changes inside either window by band or item size; it may fail if the band pattern inside the preserved window has no link to future items.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 and ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else (15 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else 0)) - (item / 2 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent two's steep tight branch with parent one's triangular peak on the loose branch: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual, so near-exact fills dominate; looser bins score their residual, favoring roomy bins, plus a triangular bonus peaking at 30 for residuals of 35 inside [25,45]. Ranking changes at the tight threshold and inside the peak window; it may fail if residuals near 35 are no more useful than the roomiest bins.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else ((r - item) + (30 - abs((r - item) - 35) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by giving both their adjustments a triangular shape: residuals in [25,45] earn a peak bonus of 30 minus distance from 35, preserving leftovers near the most useful size; residuals in [8,22] lose a valley penalty of 15 minus distance from 15, punishing the most awkward leftovers hardest. The base is plain best fit. Ranking changes inside either triangular zone; it may fail if the worst leftovers are not really near 15.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 - abs((r - item) - 35) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - (15 - abs((r - item) - 15) if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge both parents' window rules with item-scaled, residue-graded magnitudes: residuals in [28,45] gain item/2 when the item is 1 modulo 3, item/4 when it is 2 modulo 3, and nothing when it is 0 modulo 3, blending parent one's scaling with parent two's gate; residuals in [6,22] lose item/2, using the union of both penalty windows. Ranking changes across windows and item residues; it may fail if item residues carry no information about future sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (item / 2 if 28 <= r - item <= 45 and item % 3 == 1 else (item / 4 if 28 <= r - item <= 45 and item % 3 == 2 else 0)) - (item / 2 if 6 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by grading the peak with the modulo gate: residuals in [25,45] earn the full peak bonus, 30 minus distance from 35, when the item is 1 modulo 3, half otherwise; residuals in [8,22] lose 20, as in parent two. The peak matters most for one item class; the penalty applies to all. Ranking changes inside both windows by item residue; it may fail if residues carry no information about future sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((30 - abs((r - item) - 35)) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 and item % 3 == 1 else ((30 - abs((r - item) - 35)) / 2 if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0)) - (20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with the band rule, exempting the tightest bin: bins score minus residual, plus 30 in even 10-wide bands — except the single tightest bin, which never gets the bonus. An even-band bin can thus overtake the tightest choice, while the tightest bin stays protected from band-driven use. Ranking changes in the even bands away from the minimum; it may fail if the tightest bin is rarely worth protecting.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 and r > min(bins) else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's steep tight branch with parent two's windows over a best-fit loose branch: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual, so near-exact fills dominate; looser bins score minus residual plus 15 in [28,48] and minus 15 in [8,22]. Tight fills stay first, but preserved leftovers beat merely roomy bins. Ranking changes inside the windows and at the threshold; it may fail if roomy bins beat preserved leftovers.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else (-(r - item) + 15 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else (-(r - item) - 15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else -(r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's tight branch with parent two's windows, with a relative tight criterion: residuals up to half the item score 100 minus residual, rewarding fills consuming at least half the remaining space; other bins score minus residual plus 25 in [30,45] and minus 25 in [10,20]. The threshold moves with the item size. Ranking changes at the threshold and inside the windows; it may fail if the half-item criterion rarely matches the best tight choices.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= item / 2 else (-(r - item) + 25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else (-(r - item) - 25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else -(r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents through a moving window on the average leftover: the average post-placement residual is the center; residuals within 10 of it gain item/2 when the item is 1 modulo 3, blending both parents; residuals more than 20 below the center lose item/2. The window follows the current distribution. Ranking changes near the center and far below it; it may fail if the average leftover is not useful to preserve.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (item / 2 if abs((r - item) - (sum(bins) / len(bins) - item)) <= 10 and item % 3 == 1 else 0) - (item / 2 if (r - item) < (sum(bins) / len(bins) - item) - 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with parent two's two-regime shape into three regimes: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual, so near-exact fills dominate; residuals from 11 to 60 score minus residual, keeping plain best fit in the middle; residuals above 60 score their residual, spreading into nearly empty bins instead of disturbing moderately filled ones. Ranking changes at both thresholds; it may fail if the roomiest bins are better saved than spent.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else ((r - item) if r - item > 60 else -(r - item))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by grading the peak with two factors: residuals in [25,45] earn the full peak bonus, 30 minus distance from 35, only when the item is 1 modulo 3, and the residual is in an even band; half when exactly one factor matches, a quarter when neither does. Residuals in [8,22] lose 20. Height varies with class and band. Ranking changes inside the peak window by both factors; it may fail if neither factor predicts useful leftovers.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((30 - abs((r - item) - 35)) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 and item % 3 == 1 and ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else ((30 - abs((r - item) - 35)) / 2 if 25 <= r - item <= 45 and (item % 3 == 1 or ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0) else ((30 - abs((r - item) - 35)) / 4 if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0))) - (20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by flattening the peak into a plateau: residuals in [30,40] earn the full 30, tapering to 25 at edges 25 and 45, so the whole central band is equally worth preserving instead of exactly 35; residuals in [10,20] lose 25, as in parent two. The base is plain best fit. Ranking changes inside the plateau and the penalty window; it may fail if the exact center 35 is genuinely better than its neighbors.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 - max(0, abs((r - item) - 35) - 5) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - (25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's shape with parent two's windows, scaled by the square root of the item: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual; looser bins score their residual, while residuals in [28,42] gain three times the square root of the item and residuals in [6,20] lose the same. Adjustments grow with item size but with diminishing returns. Ranking changes inside the windows and at the tight threshold; it may fail if square-root scaling underweights large items.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else (r - item)) + (3 * sqrt(item) if 28 <= r - item <= 42 else 0) - (3 * sqrt(item) if 6 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents with a smooth exponential peak: residuals earn item/2 times exp of minus distance from 35 over 15 when the item is 1 modulo 3, item/4 otherwise, blending both parents; residuals in [6,22] lose item/2. The bonus decays smoothly from the center instead of jumping. Ranking changes near the peak center and inside the penalty window; it may fail if the smooth decay blurs the useful window.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((item / 2 if item % 3 == 1 else item / 4) * exp(-abs((r - item) - 35) / 15)) - (item / 2 if 6 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent two's steep tight branch with parent one's band rule, letting the band switch the loose regime: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; even-band loose bins score their residual, odd-band ones score minus residual. Band parity thus decides between worst fit and best fit. Ranking changes across bands and at the tight threshold; it may fail if the band pattern has no link to future items.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else ((r - item) if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else -(r - item))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by stacking their window adjustments: residuals in [30,45] gain 25 plus item/2, residuals in [28,30) gain item/2, and residuals in (22,28) gain item/4, keeping parent two's stepped rise; residuals in [10,20] lose 25 plus item/2, while residuals in [6,10) and (20,22] lose item/2. Stacking strengthens the adjustments where both parents agree. Ranking changes inside the windows by overlap and item size; it may fail if stacked magnitudes overcorrect.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (25 + item / 2 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else (item / 2 if 28 <= r - item < 30 else (item / 4 if 22 < r - item < 28 else 0))) - ((25 + item / 2) if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else (item / 2 if 6 <= r - item < 10 or 20 < r - item <= 22 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's relative tight criterion with parent two's windows: residuals up to half the item score 100 minus residual, rewarding fills consuming at least half the remaining space; other bins score minus residual plus item/2 in [28,42] and minus item/2 in [6,20]. Threshold and window sizes both move with the item. Ranking changes at the threshold and inside the windows; it may fail if item scaling distorts choices for extreme item sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= item / 2 else (-(r - item) + item / 2 if 28 <= r - item <= 42 else (-(r - item) - item / 2 if 6 <= r - item <= 20 else -(r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent two's shape with parent one's band rule, banding the pre-placement residual: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual; looser bins score their residual; bins in an even pre-placement band gain 30. The bonus rewards bins already in an even band, regardless of the leftover. Ranking changes in the even pre-placement bands and at the tight threshold; it may fail if pre-placement bands have no link to useful leftovers.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else (r - item)) + (30 if (r // 10) % 2 == 0 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with the band rule, but let the bonus decay with the residual: residuals in even 10-wide bands gain the larger of zero and 20 minus half the residual, so low even bands earn up to 20 while high even bands earn almost nothing; odd-band residuals gain nothing. The band reward now fades as bins get roomier. Ranking changes in the even bands by residual size; it may fail if high even bands are actually worth rewarding.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (max(0, 20 - (r - item) / 2) if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with parent two's windows by sloping them: residuals in [28,48] gain 15 plus half their distance above 28, so the largest useful leftovers earn the most; residuals in [8,22] lose 15 plus half their distance below 22, so the smallest awkward leftovers are punished hardest. The adjustments grow toward the window extremes instead of staying flat. Ranking changes inside the windows by position; it may fail if the window centers matter more than the extremes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (15 + (r - item - 28) / 2 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else 0) - (15 + (22 - (r - item)) / 2 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's tight branch with parent two's windows over a logarithmic loose branch: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual, so near-exact fills dominate; looser bins score ten times the log of one plus the residual, compressing differences among roomy bins so the windows decide there — plus 25 in [30,45] and minus 25 in [10,20]. Ranking changes inside the windows and at the tight threshold; it may fail if compressing loose-bin differences hides useful distinctions.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else (10 * log(1 + (r - item)) + 25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else (10 * log(1 + (r - item)) - 25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 10 * log(1 + (r - item))))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by scaling the peak and valley with the item: residuals in [25,45] gain item/2 times one minus distance from 35 over 10, peaking at the center; residuals in [8,22] lose item/2 times one minus distance from 15 over 7, punishing the middle hardest. Both shapes now grow with the item at stake. Ranking changes inside the triangular zones by item size; it may fail if item-scaled shapes distort choices for extreme item sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((item / 2) * (1 - abs((r - item) - 35) / 10) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - ((item / 2) * (1 - abs((r - item) - 15) / 7) if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's steep tight branch with parent two's windows over a quadratic loose branch: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; looser bins score the residual plus its square over 200, so differences among roomy bins grow with size, the windows deciding the middle — plus 25 in [30,45] and minus 25 in [10,20]. Ranking changes inside the windows and at the tight threshold; it may fail if amplifying roomy differences rewards wasteful loose bins.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else ((r - item) + (r - item) * (r - item) / 200 + 25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else ((r - item) + (r - item) * (r - item) / 200 - 25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else (r - item) + (r - item) * (r - item) / 200))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Grade the triangular peak three ways by the item's residue: residuals in [25,45] gain 30 minus distance from 35 for residue 1, 15 minus half the distance for residue 2, and nothing for residue 0; residuals in [8,22] lose 20. Ranking changes inside the peak zone by item residue; it may fail if residue classes carry no real signal about future items.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((30 - abs((r - item) - 35)) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 and item % 3 == 1 else ((15 - abs((r - item) - 35) / 2) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 and item % 3 == 2 else 0)) - (20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Center the triangular peak on the average leftover: residuals within 10 of the mean post-placement residual gain 30 minus distance from that mean when the item is 1 modulo 3, so the peak follows the distribution instead of sitting at 35; residuals more than 20 below the mean lose item/2. Ranking changes near the moving average by residue class; it may fail if the average leftover is a poor anchor.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((30 - abs((r - item) - (sum(bins) / len(bins) - item))) if abs((r - item) - (sum(bins) / len(bins) - item)) <= 10 and item % 3 == 1 else 0) - (item / 2 if (r - item) < (sum(bins) / len(bins) - item) - 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by taking the weaker magnitude per window: residuals in the overlap [28,42] gain the smaller of item/2 and 15, residuals in [43,48] gain 15; residuals in the overlap [8,20] lose the smaller of item/2 and 15, residuals in [6,7] and [21,22] lose 15. Each window uses the lesser amount where they agree. Ranking changes inside the windows by item size; it may fail if taking the minimum understates both parents' evidence.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (min(item / 2, 15) if 28 <= r - item <= 42 else (15 if 43 <= r - item <= 48 else 0)) - (min(item / 2, 15) if 8 <= r - item <= 20 else (15 if 6 <= r - item <= 7 or 21 <= r - item <= 22 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the steep tight branch with the triangular peak added to a best-fit loose branch: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; looser bins score minus the residual plus 30 minus distance from 35 inside [25,45], so the peak lifts mid-range bins above their best-fit rank without replacing the base. Ranking changes inside the peak zone and at the tight threshold; it may fail if lifting mid-range bins wastes nearly full bins.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else (-(r - item) + (30 - abs((r - item) - 35) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by crossing their magnitudes: residuals in the overlap [28,42] gain the fixed 15 while residuals in [43,48] gain item/2; residuals in the overlap [8,20] lose the fixed 15 while residuals in [6,7] and [21,22] lose item/2. Each parent's amount applies where the other parent's window extends alone. Ranking changes inside the windows by item size; it may fail if swapping the magnitudes has no basis in either parent's evidence.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (15 if 28 <= r - item <= 42 else (item / 2 if 43 <= r - item <= 48 else 0)) - (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 20 else (item / 2 if 6 <= r - item <= 7 or 21 <= r - item <= 22 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Choose the tight branch by the open-bin count: with eight or more feasible bins, residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; with fewer bins, residuals up to 12 score 100 minus the residual; looser bins always score their residual. Ranking changes at the tight thresholds by bin count; it may fail if the count threshold has no link to which tight rule works.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [((200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else (r - item)) if len(bins) >= 8 else (100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else (r - item))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with triangular windows: residuals in [28,48] gain 15 minus distance from 38, peaking at the center and fading at the edges; residuals in [8,22] lose 15 minus distance from 15, punishing the middle hardest and fading at the edges. The windows now have peaks instead of flat tops. Ranking changes inside the triangular zones; it may fail if flat windows captured the true preference better.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (15 - abs((r - item) - 38) if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else 0) - (15 - abs((r - item) - 15) if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by crossing their halves: take parent one's stepped bonus — item/2 in [28,45] and item/4 in (22,28) — and parent two's fixed penalty of 15 in [8,22]. The bonus keeps its item-scaled steps while the penalty becomes a flat amount. Ranking changes inside the bonus steps and the penalty zone by item size; it may fail if the stepped bonus and the flat penalty disagree about which leftovers matter.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (item / 2 if 28 <= r - item <= 45 else (item / 4 if 22 < r - item < 28 else 0)) - (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents into nested two-tier windows: residuals in the inner bonus window [30,45] gain 25 while residuals in the outer ring [28,30) and (45,48] gain 15; residuals in the inner penalty window [10,20] lose 25 while residuals in the outer ring [8,10) and (20,22] lose 15. Each parent supplies one tier, the larger amount inside. Ranking changes inside the nested windows; it may fail if the two-tier split has no basis in the data.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else (15 if 28 <= r - item < 30 or 45 < r - item <= 48 else 0)) - (25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else (15 if 8 <= r - item < 10 or 20 < r - item <= 22 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's steep tight branch with parent two's item-scaled windows on a worst-fit loose branch: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; looser bins score their residual, plus item/2 in [28,42] and minus item/2 in [6,20]. The tight branch rewards exactness while the windows steer the loose choices by item size. Ranking changes inside the windows and at the tight threshold; it may fail if the item-scaled windows fight the tight branch's preference.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else ((r - item) + item / 2 if 28 <= r - item <= 42 else ((r - item) - item / 2 if 6 <= r - item <= 20 else (r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by shifting the triangular peak with the item's residue: the peak center is 35 for residue 1, 30 for residue 2, and 40 for residue 0, with height 30 minus distance from the center inside [25,45]; residuals in [8,22] lose 20. The peak's favorite leftover moves with the residue class. Ranking changes inside the peak zone by item residue; it may fail if residue classes carry no real signal about future items.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 - abs((r - item) - (35 if item % 3 == 1 else (30 if item % 3 == 2 else 40))) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - (20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents with a tight-presence gate: if any feasible bin leaves a residual up to 10, use the steep tight branch with a worst-fit loose branch; if no such bin exists, use best fit with the triangular peak in [25,45]. The aggressive regime runs only when its target exists, otherwise the peak guides the choice. Ranking changes with the presence of a tight bin; it may fail if one tight bin should not change every other choice.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [((200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else (r - item)) if sum([1 for q in bins if q - item <= 10]) >= 1 else (-(r - item) + (30 - abs((r - item) - 35) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Add the band bonus to the relative-tight rule: residuals up to half the item score 100 minus the residual; looser bins score minus the residual, plus 25 in [30,45] and minus 25 in [10,20]; every residual in an even 10-wide band gains 30 more. Ranking changes inside the windows and bands by item size; it may fail if stacking the band bonus overvalues even-band leftovers.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= item / 2 else (-(r - item) + 25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else (-(r - item) - 25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else -(r - item)))) + (30 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Put the item-scaled peak and valley on the band-switched loose branch: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; looser bins score their residual in even bands and minus it in odd bands, plus an item-scaled peak in [25,45] and minus an item-scaled valley in [8,22]. Ranking changes inside the peak, valley, and bands; it may fail if stacking three adjustments overfits the search set.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else (((r - item) if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else -(r - item)) + ((item / 2) * (1 - abs((r - item) - 35) / 10) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - ((item / 2) * (1 - abs((r - item) - 15) / 7) if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by stacking the triangular peak on the flat windows: residuals in [25,45] gain 30 minus distance from 35, plus 25 more in [30,45], so the overlap gains up to 55; residuals in [10,20] lose 25. The peak and the window reinforce each other where they agree. Ranking changes inside the peak and window zones; it may fail if stacking two bonuses overvalues the middle residuals.

```python
    return [-(r - item) + (30 - abs((r - item) - 35) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) + (25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - (25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by putting the item-scaled windows on the relative-tight rule: residuals up to half the item score 100 minus the residual; looser bins score minus the residual, plus item/2 in [28,42] and minus item/2 in [6,20]. The tight threshold moves with the item while the windows scale with it too.
